title: Lean-Verified Proof of the 2009 Aaronson–Ambainis Quantum Query Conjecture
whyItMatters: Settles the 17-year-old Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture on low-degree bounded Boolean polynomials, pinning down fundamental limits on black-box quantum speedups with a complete Lean 4 proof.
summary: David Turturean at Physical Superintelligence (PSI), using an unreleased Anthropic model inside a Lean-coupled verification harness, published a proof and complete Lean 4 formalization of the 2009 Aaronson–Ambainis conjecture: every low-degree bounded polynomial on the Boolean hypercube admits an influential variable, implying any black-box quantum algorithm can be simulated classically on almost all inputs with at most a polynomial query blowup. Scott Aaronson publicly acknowledged the breakthrough, and three days later (Nov 9) Huffstutler, Miloschewsky, and Podder released a shorter independent proof.
technicalHighlights: Proves every bounded degree-d polynomial on {-1, 1}^n with non-trivial variance has a coordinate of influence at least poly(Var(f)/d).
Establishes that super-polynomial black-box quantum speedups require strong global structure (such as periodicity in Shor’s algorithm) and cannot arise from generic unstructured functions.
Released with a complete Lean 4 formalization (physical-superintelligence/aaronson-ambainis) and corroborated three days later by an independent shorter proof.
caveats: Initial preprint (arXiv:2611.09773) is not yet journal peer-reviewed; while the Lean formalization checks the formal statement against standard axioms, full community audit of the exposition and comparison with the independent Nov 9 proof are ongoing.

scoreRationale.foundational: Resolves one of the foremost open conjectures in quantum query complexity and analysis of Boolean functions since 2009.
scoreRationale.ripple: Clarifies the exact boundary between classical and quantum query power, informing quantum algorithm design and complexity theory.
scoreRationale.verification: Complete public Lean 4 formalization acknowledged by Scott Aaronson and swiftly reinforced by a shorter independent proof.
scoreRationale.velocity: Cracked a 17-year-old quantum complexity conjecture—with full Lean formalization—via an AI-driven theorem-proving harness.
